description: REQ-114's own Edge Cases text (behavioral-spec.md, the paragraph beginning 'Malformed/negative/non-finite principal_usd/repaid_usd on any row (a corrupted or adversarial ledger entry): treated as contributing 0 to both totalIssuedUsd and totalDefaultedUsd for that specific row (fail-closed — never a negative or NaN aggregate)') and the mirrored REQ-114 text for computeRecentDefaultLossUsd ('Malformed/negative/non-finite principal_usd/repaid_usd/defaulted_ms on any row contributes 0 to the sum for that specific row') are NOT actually satisfied by the current implementation when `repaid_usd` specifically (as opposed to `principal_usd`) is a negative-but-finite number. Verified empirically this session (node --input-type=module, run against the real lending-gate.mjs, not a fixture): `computeOverallDefaultRateUsd({loanRows:[{loan_id:'loan_x', status:'defaulted', principal_usd:1, repaid_usd:-5}]})` returns `{totalIssuedUsd:1, totalDefaultedUsd:6, defaultRateUsd:6, sampleSize:1}` — a defaultRateUsd of 6.0 (600%) is nonsensical and totalDefaultedUsd (6) exceeds totalIssuedUsd (1), which the spec's own text says should never happen for a malformed row (it should contribute 0 to both). Same pattern reproduced in `computeRecentDefaultLossUsd`: a row with `principal_usd:1, repaid_usd:-5` yields `totalRecentDefaultLossUsd:6` instead of `0`. The bug persists even when `principal_usd` is ALSO negative (tested `principal_usd:-5, repaid_usd:-10` → `totalDefaultedUsd:10`, `totalRecentDefaultLossUsd:5` — still nonzero, still inconsistent, `totalDefaultedUsd` exceeding `totalIssuedUsd:0`).
rootCause: In computeOverallDefaultRateUsd (lending-gate.mjs lines 245-261), `principal` is explicitly floored to 0 when negative (`finiteOr(row.principal_usd, 0) >= 0 ? finiteOr(row.principal_usd, 0) : 0`, line 251), but `finiteOr(row.repaid_usd, 0)` (line 254) is used as-is with NO equivalent floor — a negative `repaid_usd` is subtracted as a large positive contribution: `Math.max(0, principal - repaid_usd)` where `repaid_usd` is itself negative inflates rather than zeroes the row's contribution. The exact same pattern exists in computeRecentDefaultLossUsd (lines 263-273, line 270): `Math.max(0, finiteOr(row.principal_usd, 0) - finiteOr(row.repaid_usd, 0))` has no floor on either input before the subtraction — only the FINAL Math.max(0, ...) floors the net result, which is insufficient when repaid_usd's own negativity flips the sign of the subtraction.

evidence.snippet: computeOverallDefaultRateUsd: `const principal = finiteOr(row.principal_usd, 0) >= 0 ? finiteOr(row.principal_usd, 0) : 0; ... totalDefaultedUsd += Math.max(0, principal - finiteOr(row.repaid_usd, 0));` (repaid_usd never floored). computeRecentDefaultLossUsd: `sum += Math.max(0, finiteOr(row.principal_usd, 0) - finiteOr(row.repaid_usd, 0));` (neither input floored before subtraction).

impactAssessment.safetyDirection: conservative, not dangerous — the bug can only INFLATE a default-loss/default-rate monitoring signal (making evaluateOverallDefaultKillSwitch MORE likely to pause new loan issuance on corrupted input), never suppress it or allow an unsafe loan through. It is a monitoring-accuracy defect, not a money-safety/fund-loss defect.
impactAssessment.practicalExploitability: LOW under normal operation this sprint: `repaid_usd` values that flow into these two functions originate from this feature's own append-only loans.jsonl, which (per this sprint's own delivered code) is only ever set via verifyRepayment's own `credited` output — and verifyRepayment (lending-verify.mjs) only ever returns `credited: +value.toFixed(6)` where the function has already asserted `value > 0` (line 101: `if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value <= 0) return {credited:0, rejected:true}`), so a negative repaid_usd cannot arise through this sprint's own normal call path. It could only reach these two functions via a hand-corrupted/adversarially-edited loans.jsonl file, or a not-yet-built future orchestrator that writes repaid_usd from an untrusted source without going through verifyRepayment first — i.e. exactly the kind of 'corrupted or adversarial ledger entry' the spec's own Edge Case text is explicitly trying to defend against, which is why this is still worth fixing, not merely theoretical.

note: Checked verification-architecture.md's own Proof Obligations table (grep for 'malformed'/'negative'/'non-finite' near REQ-114/computeOverallDefaultRateUsd/computeRecentDefaultLossUsd): no PROP-114g/h or equivalent binding Tier-1 proof obligation requires testing malformed/negative principal_usd or repaid_usd specifically for these two functions — only REQ-101's PROP-101c (a DIFFERENT function, computeLenderAvailableUsd) has a binding malformed-input proof obligation. The behavioral-spec.md Edge Case text exists but was never converted into a corresponding PROP-114g/h Tier-1 fixture in lending-gate.test.mjs, so this gap was never caught by TDD RED/GREEN, by round-1's own fresh skeptical read, or by any of this contract's own 9 CRIT criteria. Does NOT block this round's PASS verdict (none of the 9 CRIT criteria this contract binds itself to cover this case, and the failure direction is safety-conservative, not money-losing), but is a genuine, reproducible spec-fidelity gap in a requirement (REQ-114) this sprint claims to deliver 'fully.'
resolutionRecommendation: Floor `repaid_usd` (and, for defense in depth, re-floor `principal_usd` before the subtraction in computeRecentDefaultLossUsd, which currently has no floor at all on either input) the same way `principal` already is in computeOverallDefaultRateUsd — e.g. treat a negative-or-non-finite repaid_usd as 0 for that row's contribution to both totals — and add a Tier-1 fixture (a new PROP-114g) asserting a row with negative/non-finite principal_usd OR repaid_usd contributes exactly 0 to totalIssuedUsd/totalDefaultedUsd/totalRecentDefaultLossUsd, mirroring PROP-101c's existing malformed-input discipline for computeLenderAvailableUsd.
